claim: Single-particle electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has developed into a main technique for high resolution structure determination of proteins since the resolution revolution.
source: In the short time since the resolution revolution (Kuhlbrandt, 2014), single-particle electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has developed into a main technique for high resolution structure determination of proteins (Bai et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kuhlbrandt, 2014 and Bai et al., 2015a

claim: Proteins are inevitably exposed to the atmosphere at a high surface-to-volume ratio during cryo-EM specimen preparation.
source: During this process, the protein is inevitably exposed to the atmosphere at a high surface-to-volume ratio.
evidence: Based on established understanding of the cryo-EM specimen preparation process

claim: The air-water interface is a hostile environment for proteins.
source: It has often been suggested that the air-water interface is a hostile environment for proteins (Glaeser and Han, 2017; Ramsden, 1994; Taylor and Glaeser, 2008; Trurnit, 1960; Yoshimura et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior literature

claim: Globular proteins applied to dilute buffers will eventually form an insoluble monolayer of ~10 Å thickness at the air-water interface, which means that they denature completely.
source: Numerous studies from the first half of the 20th century (reviewed by Neurath and Bull (Neurath and Bull, 1938)) have shown that globular proteins applied to dilute buffers will eventually form an insoluble monolayer of ~10 Å thickness at the air-water interface, which means that they denature completely.
evidence: Supported by citation to review by Neurath and Bull, 1938

claim: All 31 different proteins examined by electron cryo-tomography on cryo-EM grids have a more or less pronounced tendency to adhere to the air-water interface.
source: A recent systematic investigation by electron cryo-tomography (cryo-ET) of 31 different proteins on cryo-EM grids has shown that all have a more or less pronounced tendency to adhere to the air-water interface (Noble et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Noble et al., 2018

claim: Proteins diffuse from the bulk phase of a thin layer of aqueous solution to the air-water interface in a millisecond or less.
source: Proteins diffuse from the bulk phase of a thin layer of aqueous solution to the air-water interface in a millisecond or less (Israelachvili, 2011; Naydenova and Russo, 2017; Taylor and Glaeser, 2008), so that each protein can make thousands of contacts with the atmosphere during the few seconds it takes to prepare a cryo-EM grid.
evidence: Supported by citations to Israelachvili, 2011; Naydenova and Russo, 2017; Taylor and Glaeser, 2008

claim: Each protein can make thousands of contacts with the atmosphere during the few seconds it takes to prepare a cryo-EM grid.
source: Proteins diffuse from the bulk phase of a thin layer of aqueous solution to the air-water interface in a millisecond or less (Israelachvili, 2011; Naydenova and Russo, 2017; Taylor and Glaeser, 2008), so that each protein can make thousands of contacts with the atmosphere during the few seconds it takes to prepare a cryo-EM grid.
evidence: Inferred from the diffusion rate and specimen preparation time

claim: At each encounter with the air-water interface, the protein is at risk of partial unfolding.
source: At each encounter, the protein is at risk of partial unfolding.
evidence: Based on inference from the hostile nature of the air-water interface

claim: Graphene is the thinnest and strongest material known and at the same time an excellent conductor.
source: It is the thinnest and strongest material known and at the same time an excellent conductor (Geim and Novoselov, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geim and Novoselov, 2007

claim: Graphene is stable under a 300 kV electron beam.
source: It is stable under a 300 kV electron beam (Sader et al., 2013), and almost completely electron-transparent to 2.13 Å resolution (the position of the first Bragg peak) and beyond (Pantelic et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sader et al., 2013

claim: Graphene is almost completely electron-transparent to 2.13 Å resolution and beyond.
source: It is stable under a 300 kV electron beam (Sader et al., 2013), and almost completely electron-transparent to 2.13 Å resolution (the position of the first Bragg peak) and beyond (Pantelic et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pantelic et al., 2012

claim: The main problem of graphene for cryo-EM is its extreme hydrophobicity.
source: The main problem of graphene for cryo-EM is its extreme hydrophobicity.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of graphene properties

claim: The FAS complex used for cryo-EM data collection was pure and homogeneous.
source: The FAS complex used for cryo-EM data collection was pure and homogeneous, as shown by size exclusion chromatography, SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and blue-native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C

claim: Thermal shift assays indicated that the FAS complex was stable.
source: Thermal shift assays indicated that the complex was stable (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), and at 1500–3000 mU/mg it was enzymatically fully active (Fichtlscherer et al., 2000; Oesterhelt et al., 1969; Wieland et al., 1979).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: The FAS complex at 1500–3000 mU/mg was enzymatically fully active.
source: Thermal shift assays indicated that the complex was stable (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), and at 1500–3000 mU/mg it was enzymatically fully active (Fichtlscherer et al., 2000; Oesterhelt et al., 1969; Wieland et al., 1979).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citations to Fichtlscherer et al., 2000; Oesterhelt et al., 1969; Wieland et al., 1979

claim: Negative-stain EM of freshly purified FAS samples indicated that the complex was structurally intact.
source: Negative-stain EM of freshly purified FAS samples indicated that the complex was structurally intact (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A

claim: Around 90% of FAS particles in plunge-frozen, unsupported thin layers of vitrified solution on holey carbon film had suffered major structural damage.
source: Cryo-EM of the same samples in plunge-frozen, unsupported thin layers of vitrified solution on holey carbon film revealed that around 90% of the particles had suffered major structural damage (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1

claim: FAS particles in two-dimensional and three-dimensional classification lacked between one third and one half of their density or had weak density at the distal part of the beta-domes.
source: FAS particles in two-dimensional (2D) and in particular three-dimensional (3D) classification lacked between one third and one half of their density or had weak density at the distal part of the beta-domes (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B

claim: A reconstruction of ~8000 FAS particles from unsupported vitrified buffer was limited to 9.5 Å resolution according to the gold-standard 0.143 FSC criterion.
source: A reconstruction of ~8000 particles was limited to 9.5 Å resolution, according to the gold-standard 0.143 FSC criterion (Scheres and Chen, 2012) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and citation to Scheres and Chen, 2012

claim: Back-tracking of incomplete particles in the 3D classes revealed major structural defects of the protein complexes in the raw micrographs.
source: Back-tracking of incomplete particles in the 3D classes (Figure 1B) revealed major structural defects of the protein complexes in the raw micrographs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C

claim: The protein must have been damaged prior to or during cryo-EM grid preparation.
source: These observations led us to conclude that the protein must have been damaged prior to or during cryo-EM grid preparation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that intact proteins became damaged during specimen preparation

claim: All batches of purified FAS plunge-frozen by different users under different conditions showed damaged FAS complexes in all imaged areas.
source: Several batches of purified FAS plunge-frozen by different users under different conditions were examined. All experiments indicated damaged FAS complexes in all imaged areas (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Small fragments of denatured FAS were found in the areas surrounding individual complexes.
source: In most instances, small fragments of denatured FAS were found in the areas surrounding individual complexes (red arrows in Figure 2A, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—video 1

claim: FAS adhered to the two opposite surfaces of the unsupported thin layers of vitrified buffer.
source: Cryo-ET revealed that FAS adhered to the two opposite surfaces of the unsupported thin layers of vitrified buffer.
evidence: Supported by cryo-ET experimental data

claim: The lower meniscus was densely packed with adsorbed protein complexes.
source: One surface, which we refer to as the lower meniscus, was densely packed with adsorbed protein complexes.
evidence: Supported by cryo-ET experimental data

claim: The upper meniscus had only a small number of particles attached.
source: The opposite surface (the upper meniscus) had only a small number of particles attached (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Nearly all the FAS particles in contact with the air-water interface were damaged.
source: Tomographic volumes suggested that nearly all the FAS particles in contact with the air-water interface were damaged.
evidence: Supported by tomographic experimental data

claim: The particles were mostly flattened on one side and appeared incomplete.
source: The particles were mostly flattened on one side and appeared incomplete (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C

claim: The flattened regions aligned with the plane of the air-water interface.
source: The flattened regions aligned with the plane of the air-water interface.
evidence: Supported by tomographic experimental data

claim: At some point during cryo-specimen preparation, the large majority of FAS complexes encountered the air-water interface, attached to it, and the air-exposed side unfolded before vitrification.
source: Our observations thus suggest that at some point during cryo-specimen preparation, the large majority of FAS complexes encountered the air-water interface, attached to it, and the air-exposed side unfolded before vitrification.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that damaged particles have flattened regions aligned with the air-water interface

claim: One side of the FAS map from subtomogram averaging lacked density, whereas the opposite side of the complex appeared complete.
source: The final reconstruction indicated that one side of the FAS map lacked density, whereas the opposite side of the complex appeared complete (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A

claim: FAS attached with its long axis parallel to the air-water interface.
source: FAS attached with its long axis parallel to the air-water interface, which accounts for the scarcity of top views in the single-particle analysis.
evidence: Inferred from subtomogram averaging data

claim: The vectors pointing from the center of FAS complexes towards their flattened side pointed towards the air-water interface.
source: This analysis indicated clearly that the vectors pointed towards the air-water interface (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D

claim: About 86% of FAS particles at the air-water interface were extensively damaged, with one third or even half of the characteristic quaternary FAS structure weak or absent.
source: About 86% were extensively damaged, with one third or even half of the characteristic quaternary FAS structure weak or absent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: The remaining 14% of FAS particles at the air-water interface had poorly resolved densities, suggesting that even those particles that appeared intact had suffered some damage.
source: The remaining 14% had poorly resolved densities (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that even those particles on the air-water interface that appeared intact had suffered some damage.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and inference from the poor resolution

claim: Most if not all particles at or near a meniscus were damaged to a greater or lesser extent by contact with the air-water interface.
source: We conclude that most if not all particles at or near a meniscus were damaged to a greater or lesser extent by contact with the air-water interface.
evidence: Inferred from the multi-reference alignment results

claim: Bubbling air through the FAS sample completely denatured all FAS complexes.
source: Bubbling air through the sample (experiment 1) completely denatured all FAS complexes (not shown), whereas in experiments 2 and 3 a small proportion remained intact.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from experiment 1

claim: Denatured proteins were a predominant feature in all three air exposure conditions except that particles adsorbed to the carbon film remained apparently undamaged.
source: Denatured proteins were a predominant feature in all the three conditions except that particles adsorbed to the carbon film in experiment 3 (Figure 4D) were apparently undamaged.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D

claim: FAS at the air-water interface is denatured, whereas it remains intact when adsorbed to a solid substrate in liquid.
source: These results show that FAS at the air-water interface is denatured, whereas it remains intact when adsorbed to a solid substrate in liquid.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental results of the three air exposure experiments

claim: When the graphene layer was rendered hydrophilic by 1-pyrCA, FAS had a strong preference for the graphene-water interface over the air-water interface.
source: When the graphene layer was rendered hydrophilic by 1-pyrCA, FAS had a strong preference for the graphene-water interface over the air-water interface (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and Figure 5—video 1

claim: Reconstructions of FAS on hydrophilized graphene both before and after multi-reference alignment indicated that all particles were intact.
source: Reconstructions both before (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3) and after (Figure 5—figure supplement 4) multi-reference alignment indicated that all particles were intact.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3, and Figure 5—figure supplement 4

claim: The best sub-tomogram averages of FAS on hydrophilized graphene yielded maps at 24.6 Å and 17.1 Å resolution before and after masking.
source: The best sub-tomogram averages yielded maps at 24.6 Å and 17.1 Å resolution before and after masking (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5

claim: FAS does not denature on hydrophilized graphene.
source: Since few if any particles stuck to the air-water interface and multi-reference alignment did not reveal any damage, we conclude that FAS does not denature on hydrophilized graphene.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that particles on hydrophilized graphene were intact

claim: All 2D class averages of FAS on hydrophilized graphene displayed high-resolution detail and confirmed that FAS was structurally undamaged.
source: All 2D class averages displayed high-resolution detail (Figure 6A) and confirmed that FAS was structurally undamaged.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A

claim: 3D classification of FAS on hydrophilized graphene showed intact complexes with well-resolved secondary structure.
source: This was verified by 3D classification, which showed intact complexes with well-resolved secondary structure.
evidence: Supported by 3D classification experimental data

claim: The dataset of FAS on hydrophilized graphene contained only intact particles.
source: Note that this dataset contained only intact particles (Figure 6B), whereas 90% of the particles in the single-particle FAS dataset from unsupported vitrified samples had suffered major damage (Figure 1B classes 2, 3), and even the remaining 10% were compromised (Figure 1B class one and Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B

claim: Auto-refinement of FAS on hydrophilized graphene without symmetry or with imposed D3 symmetry yielded maps at 4.8 and 4.0 Å resolution, respectively.
source: Auto-refinement without symmetry (C1) or with imposed D3 symmetry yielded maps at 4.8 and 4.0 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D

claim: Local resolution estimates indicated better than 3.5 Å resolution for the rigid alpha wheel of FAS on hydrophilized graphene.
source: Local resolution estimates indicated better than 3.5 Å resolution for the rigid alpha wheel (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2

claim: A map from 8000 randomly selected particles from the dataset collected on hydrophilized graphene attained a resolution of 6.4 Å.
source: For an unbiased comparison to the 9.5 Å map obtained from FAS in unsupported vitrified buffer (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A), we randomly selected 8000 particles from the dataset collected on hydrophilized graphene. The resulting map (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B) attained a resolution of 6.4 Å, confirming that hydrophilized graphene works very much better as a substrate for single-particle cryo-EM of FAS than unsupported vitrified buffer.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B

claim: Hydrophilized graphene works very much better as a substrate for single-particle cryo-EM of FAS than unsupported vitrified buffer.
source: The resulting map (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B) attained a resolution of 6.4 Å, confirming that hydrophilized graphene works very much better as a substrate for single-particle cryo-EM of FAS than unsupported vitrified buffer.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of resolution between hydrophilized graphene (6.4 Å) and unsupported buffer (9.5 Å) with the same number of particles

claim: Particle orientation was much more evenly distributed on hydrophilized graphene, compared to unsupported vitrified buffer.
source: Finally, although not random, particle orientation was much more evenly distributed on hydrophilized graphene, compared to unsupported vitrified buffer (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4

claim: An earlier single-particle cryo-EM structure of S. cerevisiae FAS in unsupported vitrified buffer reported a resolution of 7.2 Å at the 0.5 FSC threshold and 5.9 Å at 0.143 FSC.
source: An earlier single-particle cryo-EM structure of S. cerevisiae FAS in unsupported vitrified buffer (Gipson et al., 2010) reported a resolution of 7.2 Å at the 0.5 FSC threshold and 5.9 Å at 0.143 FSC.
evidence: Supported by citation to Gipson et al., 2010

claim: The 0.5 FSC resolution estimate of the earlier FAS map was realistic.
source: Therefore, the 0.5 FSC resolution estimate of that map was realistic, as confirmed by a comparison of the FAS alpha wheel in the earlier structure to the gold-standard FSC maps in the present study (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by comparison shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5

claim: The resolution of the earlier FAS map is clearly between that of the 6.4 Å map of FAS on graphene and the 9.5 Å map of FAS in unsupported vitrified buffer.
source: The resolution of the earlier map is clearly between that of the 6.4 Å map of FAS on graphene and the 9.5 Å map of FAS in unsupported vitrified buffer, which were obtained with ∼8000 particles each.
evidence: Supported by comparison of maps shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5

claim: The better quality of the earlier FAS map is fully accounted for by the larger number of particles contributing to it, and the application of D3 symmetry.
source: The better quality of the earlier map (Gipson et al., 2010) is fully accounted for by the larger number of particles contributing to it, and the application of D3 symmetry.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of particle numbers and symmetry application

claim: The 4 Å resolution of the present FAS map from 28,000 particles on hydrophilized graphene is most likely limited by the inherent flexibility of the complex.
source: The 4 Å resolution of our present map from 28,000 particles on hydrophilized graphene is most likely limited by the inherent flexibility of the complex.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on comparison with thermophilic FAS

claim: The cryo-EM structure of a FAS complex from the thermophilic fungus Chaetomium thermophilum attained a gold standard, FSC 0.143 resolution of 4.7 Å from only ∼ 4000 particles.
source: This is implied by the cryo-EM structure of a FAS complex from the thermophilic fungus Chaetomium thermophilum (Kastritis et al., 2017), which attained a gold standard, FSC 0.143 resolution of 4.7 Å from only ∼ 4000 particles.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kastritis et al., 2017

claim: Protein complexes from thermophilic organisms are more stable than those of mesophilic origin.
source: It is well known that protein complexes from thermophilic organisms are more stable than those of mesophilic origin.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

claim: More than 100,000 particles contributed to the 7.5 Å cryo-EM structure of a FAS complex from Mycobacterium smegmatis, suggesting that the mycobacterial complex is significantly less stable.
source: By comparison, more than 100,000 particles contributed to the 7.5 Å cryo-EM structure of a FAS complex from Mycobacterium smegmatis (Boehringer et al., 2013), suggesting that the mycobacterial complex is significantly less stable.
evidence: Inferred from the large number of particles required and citation to Boehringer et al., 2013

claim: In many of the cryo-EM grids examined by electron tomography, the curvatures of the upper and lower meniscus were different.
source: In many of the cryo-EM grids examined by electron tomography (Noble et al., 2018), the curvatures of the upper and lower meniscus were different.
evidence: Supported by citation to Noble et al., 2018

claim: In the case of FAS, the less densely populated upper meniscus was more strongly curved than the lower meniscus.
source: In the case of FAS, the less densely populated upper meniscus was more strongly curved than the lower meniscus (Figure 2B, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—video 1

claim: The asymmetric distribution of protein on the upper and lower meniscus is surprising, because the grids were blotted symmetrically from both sides.
source: The asymmetric distribution of protein on the upper and lower meniscus is surprising, because the grids were blotted symmetrically from both sides.
evidence: Based on the observation of asymmetric distribution despite symmetric blotting

claim: Possibly, the more densely populated lower meniscus remained in contact with air for longer during the blotting process, so that more protein accumulated on it.
source: Possibly, the more densely populated lower meniscus remained in contact with air for longer during the blotting process, so that more protein accumulated on it.
evidence: Speculative reasoning to explain the asymmetric distribution

claim: Only a minority of the FAS particles in unsupported vitreous films retained intermediate-resolution features, whereas up to 90% were at least partly denatured by the air-water interface.
source: Our cryo-EM analysis of FAS, a soluble 2.6 MDa protein complex, revealed that only a minority of the particles in unsupported vitreous films retained intermediate-resolution features, whereas up to 90% were at least partly denatured by the air-water interface.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis

claim: Usually only a minor fraction of a large single-particle data set contributes to the final high-resolution map in recently reported high-resolution cryo-EM structures.
source: A survey of recently reported high-resolution cryo-EM structures shows that usually only a minor fraction of a large single-particle data set contributes to the final high-resolution map.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple recent cryo-EM structures

claim: 19% of particles contributed to the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor.
source: Percentages of good particles were 19% for the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor (Zhu et al., 2018); 15% for human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å (Kim and Chen, 2018); 11.8% for a 4 Å nucleosome map (Takizawa et al., 2018); 8.9% for the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase (Bai et al., 2015b); and only 5.7% for the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2018

claim: 15% of particles contributed to human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å.
source: Percentages of good particles were 19% for the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor (Zhu et al., 2018); 15% for human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å (Kim and Chen, 2018); 11.8% for a 4 Å nucleosome map (Takizawa et al., 2018); 8.9% for the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase (Bai et al., 2015b); and only 5.7% for the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kim and Chen, 2018

claim: 11.8% of particles contributed to a 4 Å nucleosome map.
source: Percentages of good particles were 19% for the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor (Zhu et al., 2018); 15% for human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å (Kim and Chen, 2018); 11.8% for a 4 Å nucleosome map (Takizawa et al., 2018); 8.9% for the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase (Bai et al., 2015b); and only 5.7% for the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Takizawa et al., 2018

claim: 8.9% of particles contributed to the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase.
source: Percentages of good particles were 19% for the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor (Zhu et al., 2018); 15% for human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å (Kim and Chen, 2018); 11.8% for a 4 Å nucleosome map (Takizawa et al., 2018); 8.9% for the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase (Bai et al., 2015b); and only 5.7% for the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bai et al., 2015b

claim: Only 5.7% of particles contributed to the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel.
source: Percentages of good particles were 19% for the 3.8 Å map of a human synaptic GABAA receptor (Zhu et al., 2018); 15% for human P-glycoprotein at 3.4 Å (Kim and Chen, 2018); 11.8% for a 4 Å nucleosome map (Takizawa et al., 2018); 8.9% for the 3.4 Å structure of human γ-secretase (Bai et al., 2015b); and only 5.7% for the 4 Å structure of a sodium channel complex from electric eel (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yan et al., 2017

claim: All the structures with low percentages of good particles were prepared in unsupported vitrified buffer.
source: All were prepared in unsupported vitrified buffer.
evidence: Based on the survey of recently reported structures

claim: These numbers suggest that up to 94% of the particles may have suffered partial denaturation at the air-water interface.
source: These numbers suggest that up to 94% of the particles may have suffered partial denaturation at the air-water interface.
evidence: Speculative inference from the low percentages of good particles

claim: If hydrophilized or otherwise functionalized graphene grids prove to work as well for other proteins to overcome denaturation at the air-water interface, a much higher proportion of particles would contribute to the final structure.
source: Future studies will show whether this is indeed the case, and whether denaturation can be avoided by using hydrophilized graphene grids, as we have shown for yeast FAS. If hydrophilized or otherwise functionalized graphene grids prove to work as well for other proteins to overcome denaturation at the air-water interface, a much higher proportion of particles would contribute to the final structure.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about future applications

claim: If hydrophilized graphene works for other proteins, this would result in a large increase in data collection efficiency and significantly better maps.
source: This would result in a large increase in data collection efficiency and significantly better maps. It would be a major boost for cryo-EM.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about the potential impact

claim: Around 90% of FAS complexes adsorbed to the air-water interface are partly denatured.
source: Around 90% of complexes adsorbed to the air-water interface are partly denatured.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cryo-ET and single-particle analysis

claim: The unfolded regions of FAS face the air-water interface.
source: We show that the unfolded regions face the air-water interface.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from subtomogram averaging and orientation analysis

claim: Denaturation by contact with air may happen at any stage of specimen preparation.
source: Denaturation by contact with air may happen at any stage of specimen preparation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that proteins make thousands of contacts with the air-water interface during preparation

claim: Denaturation at the air-water interface is completely avoided when the FAS complex is plunge-frozen on a substrate of hydrophilized graphene.
source: Denaturation at the air-water interface is completely avoided when the complex is plunge-frozen on a substrate of hydrophilized graphene.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing all particles intact on hydrophilized graphene

claim: Amorphous carbon helps to spread proteins evenly on cryo-EM grids.
source: Continuous thin layers of amorphous carbon help to spread proteins evenly on cryo-EM grids (Bai et al., 2013; D'Imprima et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2015; Schraidt and Marlovits, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bai et al., 2013; D'Imprima et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2015; Schraidt and Marlovits, 2011

claim: Amorphous carbon is far from ideal as a support film for cryo-EM because it adds background and conducts electrons poorly.
source: Amorphous carbon is, however, far from ideal as a support film for cyro-EM because it adds background and conducts electrons poorly (Brink et al., 1998; Larson et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Brink et al., 1998; Larson et al., 2011

claim: Beam-induced movement is more severe on amorphous carbon support films than on unsupported films of vitrified solutions.
source: Beam-induced movement is more severe on amorphous carbon support films than on unsupported films of vitrified solutions (Russo and Passmore, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Russo and Passmore, 2014

claim: Graphene can be rendered hydrophilic by plasma etching or non-covalent chemical doping.
source: Graphene can be rendered hydrophilic by plasma etching (Russo and Passmore, 2014) or non-covalent chemical doping, exploiting the π-π stacking interaction between graphene and aromatic planar compounds such as 1-pyrenecarboxylic acid (Pantelic et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Russo and Passmore, 2014 and Pantelic et al., 2014

claim: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include that the graphene structure is preserved.
source: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include (i) the graphene structure is preserved; (ii) surface charge can be selectively modified; (iii) the number of adsorbed particles per unit area can be tuned by adjusting the concentration of the doping chemical.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of non-covalent doping

claim: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include that surface charge can be selectively modified.
source: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include (i) the graphene structure is preserved; (ii) surface charge can be selectively modified; (iii) the number of adsorbed particles per unit area can be tuned by adjusting the concentration of the doping chemical.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of non-covalent doping

claim: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include that the number of adsorbed particles per unit area can be tuned by adjusting the concentration of the doping chemical.
source: For cryo-EM, advantages of non-covalent doping include (i) the graphene structure is preserved; (ii) surface charge can be selectively modified; (iii) the number of adsorbed particles per unit area can be tuned by adjusting the concentration of the doping chemical.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of non-covalent doping

claim: The structure of FAS is well-characterized by protein crystallography.
source: The structure of FAS is well-characterized by protein crystallography (Jenni et al., 2007; Johansson et al., 2008; Lomakin et al., 2007) and cryo-EM (Gipson et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jenni et al., 2007; Johansson et al., 2008; Lomakin et al., 2007

claim: The structure of FAS is well-characterized by cryo-EM.
source: The structure of FAS is well-characterized by protein crystallography (Jenni et al., 2007; Johansson et al., 2008; Lomakin et al., 2007) and cryo-EM (Gipson et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gipson et al., 2010

claim: The well-characterized structure of FAS makes it easy to detect and analyze which part of the complex contacts the interface and to what extent it is denatured.
source: This makes it easy to detect and analyze which part of the complex contacts the interface and to what extent it is denatured.
evidence: Inferred from the availability of well-characterized FAS structure

claim: The EM maps have been deposited in the EMDB with accession codes EMD-0178 and EMD-0179.
source: The EM maps have been deposited in the EMDB with accession codes EMD-0178 (single particle cryo-EM FAS map on graphene support) and EMD-0179 (subtomogram averaging FAS map on graphene support).
evidence: Statement of data deposition
